name: Adelie Penguin
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
call_description: Rhythmic throbbing sound during courting.
did_you_know: Like all penguins, Adelie Penguins live at sea for most of the year, swimming underwater with the aid of their flipper-like wings to catch fish.

name: Apostlebird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Rough, scratchy, discordant: 'ch-kew ch-kew'; also: nasal 'git-out' when disturbed. Copyright © Fred Van Gessel
did_you_know: The Apostlebird can also be known as the 'Grey Jumper', for its hopping gait and, because it lives in groups, it can be known collectively as the 'Happy Family' or the 'Twelve Apostles'.

name: Australasian Bittern
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: When disturbed, Australasian Bitterns disappear slowly into cover or blend into the surrounding reeds by keeping perfectly still with their neck and bill pointing skywards.

name: Australasian Darter
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Usually quiet; away from nest, makes clicking sounds, at nest, makes variety of caws, hisses and clicks.
did_you_know: Darters spread their wings and tail underwater to lure fish into the shade underneath, before spearing them with their sharp bill.

name: Australasian Figbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Loud, descending 'chiew'
did_you_know: The Figbird nests in small, semi-colonial groups, with nests often quite close together.

name: Australasian Gannet
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Australasian Grebe
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Grebes eat their own feathers and feed them to their young to prevent injury when swallowing fish bones.

name: Australasian Pipit
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Australasian Shoveler
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Usually silent but occasionally from male a soft 'toot toot' and low grunting; female a soft, husky 'quack' and chattering in flight.
did_you_know: The Australasian Shoveler is the only Australian duck with a noisy whirring flight.

name: Australian Brush-turkey
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Australian Brush-turkey chicks hatch fully feathered and can fly within a few hours.

name: Australian Bustard
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Bustards are usually silent, but males roar or boom during courtship displays.
did_you_know: If there is a plague of mice or grasshoppers, Australian Bustards will gorge themselves on the plentiful food supply.

name: Australian Hobby
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: ki-ki-ki, ki-ki-ki-ki. Mostly in flight.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Australian King-Parrot
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Loud, high-pitched whistle, with a rolling "carr-ack" call in flight.
did_you_know: Although King-Parrots appear distinctly red and green to humans, when viewed under ultraviolet light, some feathers on the wings appear with a prominent yellow glow. Many birds have four types of cone in their retina, (compared to only three in humans) and see into the ultraviolet wavelengths.

name: Australian Logrunner
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Logrunner has a loud, far-carrying call that sounds like 'be-kweek-kweek-kweek-kweek'.
did_you_know: Logrunners have a spiny tail that they use as a brace when they forage in the leaf-litter.

name: Australian Magpie
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A loud musical flute-like song, often performed as a duet or by groups. An uncommon alternative name for the Australian Magpie is Flute Bird.
did_you_know: The Australian Magpie has one of the world's most complex bird songs.

name: Australian Owlet-nightjar
call_description: The common calls consist of a loud grating chirr of either two or three notes, typically "chirr-chirr-chirr".
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Australian Painted Snipe
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Most calls are made by the female. Calls include a soft mellow 'koo-oo koo-oo' that sounds like blowing across the mouth of a bottle; a penetrating 'cook-cook-cook' can be heard at dusk and dawn; and a 'kek', 'kak' or 'kit' sound is made when disturbed
did_you_know: When threatened, the Painted Snipe performs a threat display which involves extending both wings to the ground, raising the tail and sometimes emitting a loud hiss. This display makes the bird appear larger and displays the bright colours of its plumage.

name: Australian Pelican
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Pelicans have an extremely light skeleton, weighing less than 10% of their total body weight.

name: Australian Pied Oystercatcher
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Mostly silent when feeding but may utter a whistled 'peepapeep' or 'pleep-pleep' when in flight.
did_you_know: Oystercatchers use their long, strong bills to cut open the adductor muscles (that hold the two shell halves together) of bivalve molluscs in order to eat the soft mollusc's body inside.

name: Australian Pratincole
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Sweet whistling 'weeteet' or shrill 'quirriepeet'.
did_you_know: The Australian Pratincole is also known as 'Roadrunner'. On the ground, it is like a plover, running and darting along on its long legs catching insects. However, in flight it is more like a tern, flying elegantly with long, narrow wings.

name: Australian Raven
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: The territorial call is a slow, rather high "ah-ah-ah-aaaah" with the last note drawn out.
did_you_know: There are three species of raven in Australia, and three crows. Ravens are generally bigger than crows, but other differences (e.g. range, calls) are more reliable for identifying which species is which.

name: Australian Reed-Warbler
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A rich, melodious song: 'twitchee-twitchee-twitchee-quarty-quarty-quarty'. Also loud sharp 'chat' and scolding calls.
did_you_know: The Australian Reed-Warbler's nest, which is made from and attached to reeds, is designed to keep the eggs from rolling out even when the reeds are bent down by high winds.

name: Australian Ringneck
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Call loudly and often when flying or alarmed - a mellow 'kwink-kwink-kwink-kwink' or 'kling-kling'. The Port Lincoln group is more noisy and strident. The Twenty Eight Parrot is named for its call. Also, soft chattering.
did_you_know: In Western Australia, these parrots are known as Twenty Eights, from the contact call - a whistled 'twen-ty-eight' - of Australian Ringnecks in the forests of the south-west.

name: Australian Shelduck
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A loud honking, deeper and more grunted from the male, higher and more resonant from the female, 'ong ank, ong ank'.
did_you_know: Unlike other Australian ducks, the Australian Shelduck often flies in long lines or in a 'V' formation.

name: Australian Spotted Crake
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Australian Spotted Crake most common call is a sharp, metallic double-note call. Other calls are a single-note call, descibed as querulous and given when the bird is disturbed from its nest; a chattering; and a prolonged wheezing note.
did_you_know: The Australian Spotted Crake was first scientifically described by John Gould in 1843. The first part of its Latin name, Porzana, is a local (Venetian) name for the smaller crakes. Fluminea just means 'frequenting rivers'.

name: Australian White Ibis
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Drawn-out croaks.
did_you_know: Some Australian White Ibis populations have learnt to exploit artificial foods in urban environments and are becoming pests. However, although Australian White Ibises are becoming more common in some areas, their abundance is decreasing in their natural range.

name: Australian Wood Duck
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Females have long, loud, rising: 'gnow?' while male calls are shorter and higher pitched. Flocks chatter when feeding.
did_you_know: Like other waterbirds, the Australian Wood Duck hatches with a covering of waterproof down and can enter the water almost straight away.

name: Azure Kingfisher
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Usually silent, but has high thin whistle when flying: 'pee-ee, pee-ee'.
did_you_know: The Azure Kingfisher nests in a burrow dug out of a river bank.

name: Banded Lapwing
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Loud strident calls when alarmed or for contact - a plaintive three-note call, descending in pitch: 'a-chee-chee-chee'.
did_you_know: The Banded Lapwing uses foot-tapping to disturb insects from cover, running to catch anything that moves.

name: Banded Stilt
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Yelping notes 'chowk-chowk', some wheezing calls resembling plaintive whistle.
did_you_know: Banded Stilts are highly gregarious, found in small parties to dense flocks sometimes in thousands, mainly on inland saltmarshes.

name: Bar-shouldered Dove
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A loud and distinctive 'cook coo cook coo' and a bubbling, descending call.
did_you_know: The Bar-shouldered Dove is the common street-bird in Darwin and Cairns and its calls are a well-known part of urban life.

name: Bar-tailed Godwit
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Calls include a rapid "tititi" and a sharp "kuwit" in alarm.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Barking Owl
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Barking Owl has two main calls, both distinctive and unmistakable. The first is a double-noted, dog-like "wook-wook", and the second is a wavering human-like scream.
did_you_know: The Barking Owl is named for its harsh 'barking' call but can also make a much louder, wailing cry, which has given rise to another name, the 'screaming-woman bird'.

name: Bassian Thrush
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Bassian Thrush can be heard mainly at dawn or in dull weather, its song being three notes: the first steady, the second rising briefly, and the third steady.
did_you_know: If a Bassian Thrush is disturbed it often runs a short distance and then freezes, relying for defence on the camouflage of its mottled plumage against the leaf-litter of the forest floor.

name: Beach Stone-curlew
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A repeated, mournful, wailing 'wee loo', which is higher and harsher than that of the Bush Stone-curlew. When alarmed the Beach Stone-curlew may produce a 'weal' yapping sound.
did_you_know: Beach Stone-Curlews feed mostly on crabs, hammering them open and sometimes washing them before swallowing.

name: Beautiful Firetail
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A long sad floating whistle
did_you_know: When breeding, Beautiful Firetails search for food in pairs. They scuttle around on the ground and are sometimes mistaken for mice as they rustle through the undergrowth.

name: Bell Miner
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Sweet, musical, bell-like 'tink'. All birds in a colony call all day, with calls starting just before sunrise and finishing just after sunset. Also has a 'hiccupping' note and other harsher calls.
did_you_know: Bell Miners are strongly associated with psyllid (tiny insects that feed on leaves) infestations in gum trees Eucalyptus (causing the disease called 'dieback') and may even actively farm psyllids as a food source.

name: Black Bittern
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Loud repeated cooing.
did_you_know: Black Bitterns are seen in daylight more often than other bitterns.

name: Black Currawong
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Noisy, musical 'kar-week, week-kar'
did_you_know: The Black Currawong was widely eaten in the early days of European settlement in Tasmania and said to be quite tasty.

name: Black Falcon
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Deep harsh chatter, slow whining and soft whistle; but usually silent
did_you_know: The Black Falcon is a superb flier, hanging in the air or gliding on long wings and soaring on thermals rising from the hot inland plains. When hunting, it has a spectacular high-speed stoop, diving down to level out and snatch prey from the air or the ground without landing.

name: Black Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: High-pitched, weak 'peeee', usually by breeding males.
did_you_know: Black Honeyeaters, especially females, often eat charcoal and ash at old camp-fire remains.

name: Black Kite
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The call is a descending whistle "psee-err" followed by a staccato "si-si-si-si-si".
did_you_know: The Black Kite is the most abundant raptor (bird of prey) in the world.

name: Black Swan
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: The Black Swan is the only entirely black-coloured swan in the world.

name: Black-breasted Buzzard
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Generally silent, but vocal near the nest, with yelps and soft piping.
did_you_know: Black-breasted Buzzards use stones to open eggs by picking up and dropping a stone onto the egg until it breaks.

name: Black-browed Albatross
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Gutteral gruntings.
did_you_know: Black-browed Albatrosses approach close to shore and so can be seen clearly from land, especially from cliff-tops.

name: Black-chinned Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Loud churring or scratchy 'creep-creep-creep'. Also gives beautiful, complex song.
did_you_know: When choosing hair or fur to make its nest the Black-chinned Honeyeater tends to choose pale colours, plucking the white or cream hairs from cattle and horses (and even from a cat), as well as wool from sheep.

name: Black-eared Cuckoo
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Black-eared Cuckoo is usually quiet, but in the breeding season the male calls to attract a female. The call is a piercing, drawn-out, slightly descending whistle repeated at regular intervals.
did_you_know: The Black-eared Cuckoo, like the Pallid Cuckoo, eats hairy caterpillars, which are disliked by most other birds.

name: Black-faced Cormorant
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Silent except when courting, when the male has a loud gutteral grunt and the female a soft hissing sound.
did_you_know: There are about 30 species of cormorants in the world, including five in Australia. The Black-faced Cormorant is Australia's only fully marine cormorant (often called a shag).

name: Black-faced Cuckoo-shrike
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: The call most often heard is a soft churring, often being described as a warbling "creearck".
did_you_know: Cuckoo-shrikes are neither cuckoos nor shrikes, but are so called becaues their feathers have similar patterns to those of cuckoos and their beak shape resembles that of shrikes.

name: Black-faced Monarch
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Clear whistled 'why-you-whichye-oo'; also creaks, chatters and scolds.
did_you_know: Like other monarchs and flycatchers, the Black-faced Monarch has bristles around its bill to help it catch insects.

name: Black-faced Woodswallow
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Soft sweet calls; also lively song which includes mimicry and scratchy 'chiff chiff' calls.
did_you_know: During droughts, the Black-faced Woodswallow may be seen in coastal areas where it is not normally found, such as Kangaroo Island in South Australia or the Illawarra region, New South Wales.

name: Black-fronted Dotterel
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Sharp 'tip' call, singular or repeated three or four times.
did_you_know: The Black-fronted Dotterel is normally seen in small numbers, usually in pairs, sometime alone and rarely more than five. However in winter they can form larger groups of a hundred or more.

name: Black-headed Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: The contact call is a high sharp two-note whistle: 'tsip-tsip'; also a harsh churring: 'shirp-shirp-shirp'.
did_you_know: The Black-headed Honeyeater can be seen in mixed winter flocks with the Strong-billed Honeyeater, as well as pardalotes and thornbills.

name: Black-necked Stork
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Gutteral grunts. Will also clack and snap bill.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Black-shouldered Kite
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Harsh wheezing 'scaarrp'; also clear 'chee' calls in flight and while hovering.
did_you_know: Male Black-shouldered Kites feed females in mid-air during courtship. The female flips upside-down and accepts the food from the male, while the two birds are locked briefly together in flight with their feet holding the prey.

name: Black-tailed Native-hen
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Usually silent, with a single sharp alarm call: 'kak'.
did_you_know: The Black-tailed Native-hen is nomadic, taking advantage of temporary wetlands. When breeding conditions are good, large numbers of birds may suddenly arrive in an area, breed and then disappear again.

name: Black-winged Stilt
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Black-winged Stilts give a repeated high-pitched barking call.
did_you_know: Black-winged Stilts, like many shorebirds, don't swim while feeding. They feed by pecking at food items while wading in the water.

name: Blue Bonnet
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Blue Bonnets have quite a range of calls, only some of which are mentioned here. There is a Chip-chip call, which is the most useful for identification. It has been described as a harsh abrupt "jak, jakajag" or "cluck-cluck….cluk-cluck….cluck-cluck". It i
did_you_know: The Blue Bonnet can be extremely aggressive to other birds when kept in an aviary and has been known to kill birds larger than itself. The scientific name Northiella comes from Alfred John North, an ornithologist who worked at the Australian Museum. The Naretha subspecies Northiella haematogaster narethae is specially protected in WA.

name: Blue-billed Duck
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Usually silent except in display when male utters rapid, low pitched rattling sounds and the female a soft low 'quack'.
did_you_know: The tail of the Blue-billed Duck is usually held flat on the water, However, during courtship, or when alarmed, it is held fully erect.

name: Blue-faced Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Noisy, varied calls. Repeated, penetrating 'woik'; 'weet weet weet' at daybreak; also squeaks uttered during flight and softer 'hwit hwit' calls.
did_you_know: The Blue-faced Honeyeater is one of the first birds heard calling in the morning, often calling 30 minutes before sunrise.

name: Blue-winged Kookaburra
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Loud maniacal screeching cackle developing into loud trills and then ending abruptly. Also a variety of trills, 'ow' notes, barks and hoarse screeches. Often call in groups from a high perch.
did_you_know: Blue-winged Kookaburra family groups are often larger than those of the Laughing Kookaburra, with up to 12 members.

name: Blue-winged Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The call of the Blue-winged Parrot is an extremely high, thin tinkling sound, in fast, followed by slow bursts. It sounds more like the highest squeaks of a thornbill or fairy-wren than a parrot.
did_you_know: When choosing nest sites, Blue-winged Parrots try to get one with a small opening that will prevent predators, like Grey Shrike-thrushes , getting in to steal the eggs and young.

name: Bourke's Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: In flight, Bourke's Parrot makes a mellow, soft, chirruping twitter. Its alarm call is a shrill double note.
did_you_know: Another name for Bourke's Parrot is 'Night Parrot', as it will fly into watering places at night. However it is not to be confused with the real, and extremely rare, Night Parrot , Pezoporus occidentalis .

name: Brahminy Kite
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Usually silent. Drawn-out descending wail, like a bleating lamb: 'pee-ah-ah-ah'; meowing notes.
did_you_know: Brahminy Kites have weak feet so, although they have long, sharp curved claws, they cannot take large prey. However they are expert at snatching prey in flight.

name: Broad-billed Sandpiper
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Trilling 'chree-eep' in flight
did_you_know: Sandpipers belong to the family Scolopacidae, which is the largest wader family in the world and includes curlews, godwits, and snipe. Juveniles hatch in the northern hempisphere summer and migrate to the Southern Hempisphere, where they remain until they are more than a year old before returning to their breeding areas.

name: Brolga
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: The Brolga's call is a loud trumpeting 'garooo' or 'kaweee-kreee-kurr-kurr-kurr-kurr-kurr-kurr', which is given in flight, at rest or during courtship.
did_you_know: The Brolga is one of Australia's two crane species, and is known for its spectacular dance displays by both sexes during breeding season.

name: Brown Cuckoo-Dove
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The call is a haunting and distinctive 'coo-cu-woot' rising at the end. Sounds like: 'did you walk?'
did_you_know: The very long graduated tail helps the Brown Cuckoo-Dove to balance as it hangs from branches and moves in the canopy, searching for fruit.

name: Brown Falcon
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Normally silent at rest, but gives some cackling and screeching notes when in flight.
did_you_know: Falcons (Family Falconidae) lack a clutching foot mechanism to catch and kill prey, which characterises eagles, kites and relatives in the Family Accipitridae. Instead, they have powerful hooked bills with specialised 'teeth' and matching notches which can sever neck bones with one bite.

name: Brown Gerygone
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Brisk, incessant: 'which-is-it-is-it'; also soft calls.
did_you_know: The generic name Gerygone means 'born of song', referring to the sweet voices of birds in this genus.

name: Brown Goshawk
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A loud, rising 'keek-keek-keek'; also a slow, drawn out 'ee-you-wick, ee-you-wick'. Females have deeper voices than males.
did_you_know: Brown Goshawks hunt for starlings and house sparrows by flying low over towns and suburban areas in the evenings, when these birds are returning to their roosts.

name: Brown Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Clear, ringing, musical: 'whit, whit, whitchit'
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Brown Quail
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Double-noted, ascending whistle: 'pi-pieer'; also sharp alarm chirp.
did_you_know: A group of quails is called a covey.

name: Brown Songlark
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The male Brown Songlark is the singer. The continuous song is musical and metallic, produced from perches and when rising steeply above breeding territory, then fluttering in slow downward display flights between trees, ending with a whip-crack sound.
did_you_know: Male Brown Songlarks engage in 'song flights'; singing continuously as they fly up above their territories.

name: Brown Thornbill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Rich, musical warbles and accomplished mimicry; responds to imitation of calls by humans.
did_you_know: The Brown Thornbill will respond to humans imitating its calls.

name: Brown Treecreeper
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The Brown Treecreeper has a loud 'spink' call, which is given either singly or in a series, and normally betrays its presence before the bird is seen.
did_you_know: Brown Treecreepers are highly sociable birds, living and breeding communally. Each year, the previous year's offspring will remain to help the breeding male feed the female and rear new chicks. Interestingly, it is usually only males which remain to perform this duty.

name: Brown-headed Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Sharp, scratchy 'chwik-chwik-chwik'; frequently call in flight.
did_you_know: The Brown-headed Honeyeater prefers the lightest-coloured hairs for its nest, choosing white rather than brown hairs from piebald (two-tone) ponies and cattle, and ignoring all-brown animals.

name: Brush Bronzewing
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: low repeated hoop or whoo, can continue for minutes
did_you_know: 15 nests with 29 eggs were watched to see the outcome and only 3 chicks survived to leave the nest.

name: Brush Cuckoo
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Descending series of loud whistled notes: 'fear-fear-fear-fear'. Also, three note call: 'where's-the-tea'.
did_you_know: The Brush Cuckoo's eggs can match those of the host birds' in colouring and size.

name: Budgerigar
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The contact call is a warbling "chirrup"; "zit" is given in alarm.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Buff-banded Rail
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Loud creaky squeak when breeding but usually silent.
did_you_know: The Buff-banded Rail is secretive but not shy and may be seen in places like the Royal Botanic Gardens in Sydney. It darts into cover when disturbed and the young will scurry into cover when adults give an alarm call.

name: Buff-rumped Thornbill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The Buff-rumped Thornbill has a number of calls. Its song is described as: an animated rapid rattle on two notes, jingling and 'fairy-like'; or as  a rapidly repeated musical tinkling on two alternating notes. It also has a Chip call.
did_you_know: Buff-rumped Thornbills are usually found in small groups of up to 20 and are quite gregarious. They generally form larger groupings, or clans, in the non-breeding season, but split up into smaller groups in the breeding season.

name: Bush Stone-curlew
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: The voice is a characteristic drawn-out, mournful "wer-loooo", often heard at dusk and during the night
did_you_know: Bush Stone-curlews were formerly found in the fertile, shale-soiled areas of Sydney - the Cumberland Plain - but are now absent and are listed as threatened in New South Wales because of land clearing practices.

name: Cape Barren Goose
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: On the ground usually quiet unless alarmed or in display. In flight more vocal, male has higher pitched, harsh trumpeted 'ark, ark-ark'.
did_you_know: The Cape Barren Goose is able to drink salty or brackish water, allowing many of them to remain on offshore islands all year round.

name: Carnaby's Black-Cockatoo
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: Noisy with distinctive "wy-lah" call, with much variation
did_you_know: Cockatoos may move along a branch, biting off cones or seeds and green branches for no apparent reason.

name: Caspian Tern
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Common calls include a deep barky 'kah' or 'krah' and higher, squealed calls: 'ai-air-arrk'.
did_you_know: The Caspian Tern is the largest tern (60cm) and is nearly as long as the Kelp Gull (62 cm), however at least 6 cm of its length is in the tail.

name: Cattle Egret
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Usually silent, but will make croaking noises in breeding colonies
did_you_know: The Cattle Egret sits on the backs of cattle to look out for insects to eat.

name: Channel-billed Cuckoo
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
call_description: The call of the Channel-billed Cuckoo, a loud 'kawk' followed by a more rapid, and weaker 'awk-awk-awk...', is as distinctive as the bird's appearance. The call may be given when perched, but is most often given in flight.
did_you_know: The Channel-billed Cuckoo is the largest parasitic cuckoo in the world.

name: Chestnut Teal
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Sharp whistles and grunts (males) and chuckling quacks (females); very similar to Grey Teal but male calls are deeper.
did_you_know: The Chestnut Teal is sexually dimorphic. This means that males and females have quite different plumages. The related Grey Teal is not dimorphic, with both sexes appearing the same.

name: Chestnut-breasted Mannikin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Bell-like or drawn-out: 'teet'.
did_you_know: Native Australian finches belong to the Family Passeridae, while the introduced 'true' finches (the Goldfinch and Greenfinch) belong to the Family Fringillidae.

name: Chestnut-crowned Babbler
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Contact call a penetrating 'we-chee chee chee'. Short alarm call. Chatters when engaged in group activity.
did_you_know: In addition to brood nests, Chestnut-crowned Babblers build communal roosting nests of twigs and sticks in dead or partly living trees.

name: Chestnut-rumped Thornbill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Long penetrating chirping from tree tops or repeated quiet chirps while feeding. Sometimes mimics.
did_you_know: In heat of day Chestnut-rumped thornbills have been seen sheltering inside roadside culverts where it is cooler.

name: Cicadabird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Usually silent. Harsh cicadalike buzzing mainly in breeding season. In north queensland calls are different, being a loud low pitched call
did_you_know: When Cicadabirds eat they swallow insects head first, sometimes after repositioning the insect in their bill by using a branch as a support.

name: Cockatiel
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Although mostly silent, the Cockatiel gives a long and distinctive "queel-queel" in flight. It does not have the screeching voice of many other parrots and may learn to 'speak'.
did_you_know: The Cockatiel does not have the screeching voice of many other parrots and may learn to 'speak'.

name: Collared Sparrowhawk
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A rapid, almost trilled 'keek, keek, keek' and a soft mewing 'wit wit'. They are silent when hunting.
did_you_know: Collared Sparrowhawks rely on trees or tall shrubs for cover to ambush their prey, darting out to catch small birds. At other times they sit quietly and are very easily overlooked.

name: Comb-crested Jacana
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: At a distance, the Comb-crested Jacana looks like it can walk on water. In fact, it is walking on floating plants. Its extremely long toes help it to spread its body weight over a larger area.

name: Common Blackbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A repeated 'tchook' call and a melodious, warbling song.
did_you_know: The Common Blackbird is one of two introduced 'true thrushes' in Australia; the other is the Song Thrush, T. philomelos . The indigenous thrushes are the Bassian, Zoothera lunulata , and the Russet-tailed Thrush, Z. heinei .

name: Common Bronzewing
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The common call is a deep "oom", repeated several times.
did_you_know: Bronzewings, like other pigeons, secrete a special milk-like substance from their crop, which is fed to the young chicks.

name: Common Greenshank
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Clear ringing 'tchu - tchu-tchu' call
did_you_know: The Greenshank will often stalk fish or shrimps before making a rapid dash to snatch a feed. They are also sometimes seen stirring up the bottom with their feet to disturb prey and then swinging their bills from side to side to catch them.

name: Common Myna
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: The voice is unpleasant: a collection of growls and other harsh notes.The noise from large groups of Common Mynas can be deafening.
did_you_know: The Common Myna's success is mostly a result of its opportunistic behaviour and aggressiveness towards other species, bullying them around food sources and out competing them for nesting sites.

name: Common Noddy
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Common Sandpiper
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A 'tee-tee-tee' call; also a 'tittering' and trailing note call which is heard mainly during breeding
did_you_know: When feeding, the Common Sandpiper will pause to bob its head and teeter. When disturbed it will fly low preferably over water with down-curved, flicking wings. Sometimes it is called 'Bob'.

name: Common Starling
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The song of the Common Starling is an unmusical collection of wheezy whistles, clicks, scratching notes and some mimicry of other bird calls.
did_you_know: Flocks of Common Starlings are often seen at dusk wheeling in large circles as they search for a roosting site for the night

name: Common Tern
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Common calls include a long, grating 'keeee-yah' and a brisk 'kik-kik-kik'.
did_you_know: One exhausted bird picked up on a beach near Fremantle, Western Australia in 1956, had been banded as a nestling in Sweden, and in 6 months had travelled some 20,900km around the Cape of Good Hope.

name: Crescent Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Loud 'egypt' or 'eejik' calls; males have melodic song.
did_you_know: Crescent Honeyeaters show long-term fidelity to breeding sites over several years, with some birds found close to the territory where they themselves hatched.

name: Crested Bellbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Loud, liquid call. Bell-like 'did-did did-did-dit'. The calls are sometimes ventriloqual.
did_you_know: The nests of Crested Bellbirds often have live, hairy caterpillars placed around the rim. it has been suggested that the adults gather them as a food storage for the sitting bird or as a defence for the nest.

name: Crested Pigeon
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: When flying,a whistling sound is produced by the air passing over a modified primary feather on the Crested Pigeon's wing.

name: Crested Shrike-tit
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Repeated plaintive whistle: 'keep-keep-keep'; can be ventriloquial and often mimics other species.
did_you_know: Crested Shrike-tits may be heard tearing at the bark of trees, looking for insects to eat.

name: Crested Tern
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Most common calls are a raspy 'kirrick' or 'krrow'.
did_you_know: Terns are related to gulls, but have straighter, more pointed bills and more slender wings. They also have forked tails and graceful flight patterns, earning them their former name of 'sea-swallows'.

name: Crimson Chat
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: High-pitched 'see', soft 'dik-it, dik-it' or brisk 'check check'.
did_you_know: Crimson Chat, one or both parents will fake an injury on the ground in a distraction display to draw the predator away. It is also known as a 'rodent-run'.

name: Crimson Finch
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Noisy flocks, brittle tinkling, loudest of all finches.  Squeezing, rasping, nasal sounds ending with 3 decending notes. ra ra ra ra reee reee reee.
did_you_know: White Bellied subspecies (Neochmia phaeton evangelinae ) - listed as Vulnerable Nationally and Endangered in Queensland

name: Crimson Rosella
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: The Crimson Rosella has a range of calls, the commonest being a two-syllabled "cussik-cussik". It also has a range of harsh screeches and metallic whistles.
did_you_know: Crimson Rosellas are not only red, but can be yellow or orange. Yellow and red birds produce orange offspring.

name: Curlew Sandpiper
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Rippling contact call: 'chirrip, chirrip, chirrip'.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Diamond Dove
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Soft falsetto coo-oo, 'oh-my-papa' also plantive slow high pitched coo-cooooo.
did_you_know: Doves need water as they have a dry seed diet and they can suck up water without lifting their heads

name: Diamond Firetail
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Often call from dead branches with a mournful double whistle 'twooo-hee'.
did_you_know: During courtship, the male Diamond Firetail holds a long piece of green grass in his bill, then flies to a branch where he sits near the female and begins to bob up and down. When she approaches, he twists his neck around and opens his bill just like young begging for food.

name: Dollarbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The distinctive, harsh 'kak-kak-kak' call is repeated several times, and is often given in flight.
did_you_know: The origin of the Dollardbird's name stems from the silvery, circular patches on the underside of the wings, thought to resemble the American silver dollar coin.

name: Double-banded Plover
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Loud far-carrying 'pit', low double 'chip chip', soft low sliding upwards 'kwereep'.
did_you_know: The Double-banded Plover is the only migratory bird visiting Australia that breeds in New Zealand. All the others breed in the Northern Hemisphere.

name: Double-barred Finch
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A brassy, drawn-out 'tzeeaat, tzeeaat'; also a low 'tat tat'
did_you_know: The nestlings of Double-barred Finches beg with their heads down to one side. This is unique to the grass-finch and waxbill family.

name: Dusky Moorhen
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Sharp guttural crowing or harsh shrieks.
did_you_know: The Dusky Moorhen does not dive when feeding; its tail is always visible above the water when upended.

name: Dusky Robin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Far-carrying 'choo-wee, choo-we-er', repeated.
did_you_know: The Dusky Robin may sometimes breed co-operatively, with non-parent birds helping in the rearing of chicks.

name: Dusky Woodswallow
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Brassy chirrups and chirps: 'vut vut'; also harsh chattering and some mimicry.
did_you_know: Dusky Woodswallows swivel their tails in a 'tail wag' that is typical of the whole woodswallow group.

name: Eastern Barn Owl
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Barn Owls are generally quiet, the common call being a 12 second rough, hissing screech. Less frequently, birds give whistling and wheezing notes and some snapping and bill clacking during mating and threat displays.
did_you_know: Subspecies of the Barn Owl are found on every continent in the world except Antarctica.

name: Eastern Curlew
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: In flight and on the ground, a loud sad-sounding 'cuuuur-lee', rising in pitch.
did_you_know: Eastern Curlews have very long legs, allowing them to wade in boggy areas and moorland in their breeding region, where other shorter-legged waders are unable to go.

name: Eastern Grass Owl
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Usually silent. A harsh rasping screech perhaps used when a threat present. During courtship there is soft twittering and chirruping; also uttered by the male in flight returning to the nest with food.
did_you_know: The female Grass Owl is larger than the male.

name: Eastern Great Egret
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: The Eastern Great Egret is the largest of the Australian egrets.

name: Eastern Koel
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: The male Common Koel advertises its presence by a loud ascending whistle or 'koo-el', monotonously repeated; the call of the female is a repetitive 'keek-keek-keek-keek'. Males often call throughout the day and well into the night.
did_you_know: The Common Koel is being surveyed for Birds in Backyards this spring. Visit the Koel survey page for details.

name: Eastern Osprey
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Ospreys are noisy when flying in pairs or around the nest, but mainly silent when alone. The call is a repeated reedy whistle or harsh screams.
did_you_know: The Osprey has oily plumage, so that when it dives or plunges under the water for fish, its feathers become less wet and it can take off again. It does not need to spread its wings to dry, unlike cormorants.

name: Eastern Reef Egret
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: A loud croak.
did_you_know: The two colour forms of the Eastern Reef Egret interbreed, and both white and dark offspring can be found in the same brood.

name: Eastern Rosella
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: A sharp repeated 'chut-chit-chut' in flight and a high-pitched 'pee-pt-eee' or 'kwink kwink' when perched.
did_you_know: The Eastern Rosella uses one of its feet (usually the right foot) to hold food when eating on the ground or perched on a tree.

name: Eastern Spinebill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Short, repeated, high-pitched piping.
did_you_know: The Eastern Spinebill sometimes hovers like a hummingbird when feeding on the nectar from flowers. Most Australian honeyeaters feed on flowers from a perched position.

name: Eastern Whipbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Male: drawn out whip crack; female: a sharp "choo-choo".
did_you_know: The Whipbirds' long whip call, one of the most characteristic sounds of the Australian bush, is performed as a duet. The male makes the drawn out whip crack and the female usually follows quickly with a sharp "choo-choo".

name: Eastern Yellow Robin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The voice includes a variety of high bell-like piping, a repeated "chop chop" and some scolding notes.
did_you_know: Eastern Yellow Robins belong to the genus Eopsaltria which translates as 'dawn-harper'. Appropriately, they are among the first birds to be heard at dawn.

name: Eclectus Parrot
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Screeching squawking contact call in flight, but while feeding infrequently call 'chu-wee, chu-wee', also a variety of chuckling and bell-like sounds.
did_you_know: Eclectus Parrots are noisy and conspicuous, calling as they fly and screeching loudly when disturbed.

name: Elegant Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: This birds calls are poorly known, but it has "contact" and "alarm" calls and occasionally makes a soft twitterings, 'tsit'.
did_you_know: Elegant parrots can be fairly high fliers. If persistently chased in open country they can fly so high as to be out of sight. When coming in to drink they can drop straight down from a considerable height.

name: Emperor Penguin
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The call of the Emperor Penguin is described as a rhythmic and powerful buzzing chatter "a-a-a-a-a-…"
did_you_know: Penguin species of the Antarctic regions tend to be larger and rounder than those of the more temperate regions, as bulkier bodies retain heat more efficently than slimmer bodies.

name: Emu
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Booming, drumming and grunting. Booming is created in an inflatable neck sac, and can be heard up to 2 km away.
did_you_know: The name 'emu' is not an Aboriginal word. It may have been derived from an Arabic word for large bird and later adopted by early Portuguese explorers and applied to cassowaries in eastern Indonesia. The term was then transferred to the Emu by early European explorers to Australia.

name: Eurasian Coot
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The most common call is a distinctive loud "kowk".
did_you_know: The Eurasian Coot is able to compress its feathers and squeeze out all of the air, which allows it to dive deeply and for longer periods.

name: Eurasian Skylark
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: High-pitched, musical warbling often continuous during flight. During song flight, the males fly high in the air, singing melodiously.
did_you_know: The Skylark was introduced from Britain in the 1850s. It is known for its beautiful song, often given in flight.

name: European Goldfinch
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A liquid 'tu-leep' or 'tsi-i-it'; also twittering song.
did_you_know: A group of Goldfinches is called a 'charm'.

name: Fairy Martin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Soft, churing notes and twittering.
did_you_know: The Fairy Martin is known as the 'Bottle Swallow' for its characteristic bottle-shaped mud nests, often made in cliffs or under bridges and culverts.

name: Fairy Tern
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Varied; common calls include a throaty 'krik-krik-krik' and a high-pitched, scolding 'kekekeket'.
did_you_know: Huge flocks of Fairy Terns have been seen along the north-western Australian coast by aerial fisheries observers. Individual flocks may contain up to two or three thousand birds, and one flock was estimated to contain as many as 15,000 birds.

name: Fan-tailed Cuckoo
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A mournful, descending trill.
did_you_know: The egg of a cuckoo tends to hatch earlier than those of its host, which allows the cuckoo chick to remove the unwanted eggs of its 'adopted' parents.

name: Flame Robin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Flame Robins have an attractive song. The high-pitched musical trill has three sets of three notes, which have been interpreted as "you may come if you wish to the sea".
did_you_know: Flame Robins are the only robins to form flocks in winter.

name: Flesh-footed Shearwater
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The Flesh-footed Shearwater has a number of calls, but it is generally silent at sea. Its main call starts with a "gug-gug-gug" to be followed witth a hoarse asthmatic crooning "ku-koo-ah" with stress on the middle sound and last being like a sob. This cr
did_you_know: Flesh-footed Shearwaters can nest in the same area as Great-winged Petrels,Pterodroma macroptera. The latter breed in winter while the Shearwaters breed in summer. Both will use the same burrow but if one pair rears a chick the other will usually be prevented from using that burrow in the following season.

name: Forest Kingfisher
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A series of rapidly repeated notes, either a high pitched whistle: 'krree-krree-krree' or a 'machine gun' call; also harsh strident chatter near the nest.
did_you_know: During nest-making Forest Kingfishers fly with such force into the termite nest that deaths from a broken neck have sometimes been seen.

name: Forest Raven
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Slow baritone 'korr...korr...korr' ( not the wail of the Australian Raven). Points tail downwards when it calls.
did_you_know: The Forest Raven is the only corvid (crow or raven) that occurs in Tasmania.

name: Forty-spotted Pardalote
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A soft double note, harsher than that of Spotted Pardalote.
did_you_know: The Forty-spotted Pardalote is one of Australia's rarest birds.

name: Freckled Duck
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: As a contact call a soft musical piping. Alarm call a flute like 'wheeooo'. At nest, in display, loud discordant 'quacks'.
did_you_know: During the breeding season, the male Freckled Duck’s bill becomes crimson at the base.

name: Fuscous Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: A rolling chitter: 'arig arig a taw taw'; also deep metallic flight song 'tew-tew-tew', and contact call is short 'jeow'.
did_you_know: Fuscous Honeyeaters are often found in association with rosellas, as well as with other nectar-eating honeyeaters e.g. White-naped Honeyeaters, aerial-feeding insect-eating birds e.g. Willie Wagtails, Restless Flycatchers and Dusky Woodswallows, and larger insect-eaters e.g Grey Shrike-thrushes.

name: Galah
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The voice is a distinctive high-pitched screech, 'chi-chi'.
did_you_know: Galahs can breed with other members of the cockatoo family, including the Sulphur-crested Cockatoo, C. galerita .

name: Gang-gang Cockatoo
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Creaky, rising screech that sounds like a rusty hinge: 'ky-or-ark'. A soft growling is made when feeding.
did_you_know: Gang-gang Cockatoos almost always use their left foot to hold food when eating.

name: Glossy Black-Cockatoo
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Noisy squawks or creaky calls; wheezy call-notes. Quieter and less raucous than other black-cockatoos.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Glossy Ibis
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: During flight, utters a 'thu-thu-thu-u' call.
did_you_know: The Glossy Ibis is the smallest of the three species of ibis in Australia, and habitually nest in the shelter of other, larger species.

name: Golden Whistler
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The Golden Whistler's voice is strong, musical and varied. Songs include a "we-we-we-tu-whit", the last note be stronger and whip-like, and a rising "seep"
did_you_know: The Golden Whistler belongs to the Family Pachycephalidae, which means 'thick-head' after the group's robust necks and heads. This species is one of Australia's loudest and most beautiful songsters.

name: Golden-headed Cisticola
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Metallic, fluid buzzing calls, soft peeping and harsh scolding alarm calls. In breeding season calls almost continuously.
did_you_know: The Golden-headed Cisticola sews leaves together to form part of its nest, giving it its other common name: Tailorbird.

name: Gouldian Finch
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The Gouldian Finch is mostly silent, although a high-pitched whistling "ssitt", may be uttered from time to time.
did_you_know: The Gouldian Finch is the only grassfinch that nests exclusively in tree hollows or holes in termite mounds.

name: Great Cormorant
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: The Great Cormorant is the largest of the Australian cormorants and is one of the largest in the world.

name: Great Crested Grebe
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Calls of the Great Crested Grebe are described as a guttural 'karr-arr', a shrill 'er-wick', as well as trumpeting, moaning and whirring noises.
did_you_know: Grebes are expert divers, and usually dive rather than fly to escape danger.

name: Great Knot
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Usually silent. Double noted whistle in flight.
did_you_know: Great Knots start to breed around the age of two years.

name: Green Catbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Cat-like mewing; sometimes likened to the cry of a human baby.
did_you_know: Although they belong to the bowerbird family, male Green Catbirds do not build bowers and only mate with one female, helping her to defend and feed their offspring.

name: Green Rosella
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: Often call in flight with a distinctive 'kzink' or 'krissk'. They also have a very high ringing call, with the second note highest, and harsh, typical rosella chattering.
did_you_know: The Green Rosella is Australia's largest rosella and occurs only in Tasmania and the Bass Strait islands.

name: Grey Butcherbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The song is a lovely rich piping with some mimicry and harsher notes.
did_you_know: Butcherbirds get their name from their habit of hanging captured prey on a hook or in a tree fork, or crevice. This 'larder' is used to support the victim while it is being eaten, to store several victims or to attract mates.

name: Grey Currawong
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: High-pitched ringing, clinking call.
did_you_know: The Grey Currawong is so diverse in appearance that its six subspecies were originally thought of as separate species.

name: Grey Fantail
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Ascending, tinkling, whistles and squeaks.
did_you_know: The nest of the Grey Fantail has a long tapering stem that resembles a wine-glass.

name: Grey Goshawk
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Males have a high, piercing 'kieek-kieek', repeated 10 - 20 times, while female calls slower and mellower, with most calls made during breeding.
did_you_know: The white form of the Grey Goshawk is the only pure white raptor in the world.

name: Grey Plover
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Generally silent in Australia; 'kliooee' call in the north.
did_you_know: When the Grey Plover feeds it it has a hunched stance and lethargic behaviour giving it a dejected appearance.

name: Grey Shrike-thrush
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The Grey Shrike-thrush has a varied, rich and melodious voice. The call varies throughout its range and between individuals, but typical phrases include "pip-pip-pip--pip-hoee", "pur-pur-pur-kwee-yew", and a sharp "yorrick".
did_you_know: Grey Shrike-thrush pairs mate for life and maintain breeding territories of up to 10 hectares.

name: Grey Teal
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Grey-crowned Babbler
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Loud scolding and chattering calls: 'wee-oo'. Also distinctive 'ya-hoo' duet by breeding female ('yah') and male ('ahoo') repeated six to eight times.
did_you_know: The old nests of Grey-crowned Babblers are used by a variety of other birds: Blue-faced Honeyeaters sometimes nest on top of the dome. Yellow-rumped Thornbills may nest underneath and are even tolerated in active nests.

name: Grey-tailed Tattler
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: An upslurred whistle 'tu-whip'.
did_you_know: The nest of the Grey-tailed Tattler were not discovered by humans until 1959. It was simply a hollow among stones, lined with dried grass. The sitting female was very tame and allowed the observer, a Russian geologist, to approach within arm's length.

name: Ground Parrot
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Ground Parrot calls at dawn and dusk. The call consists of piercing, ringing, resonating whistles, rising in steps. They also warble in sharp, rapid trills like a budgie.
did_you_know: Ground Parrots prefer to run rather than fly away. They fly short distances and then run through the dense undergrowth.

name: Gull-billed Tern
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Varied; common calls include a loud metallic 'gaa-gaa-gaa', a soft nasal 'kek-kek' and a stuttered 'kerrrr'.
did_you_know: The Gull-billed Tern rarely occurs over the ocean, being an inland species over most continents except Antarctica.

name: Hall's Babbler
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The Hall's Babbler constantly calls or 'clucks' while foraging, and has a loud 'buzz' alarm call that usually results in all the birds taking refuge in nearby trees.
did_you_know: The Hall's Babbler was only identified as a separate species in 1964, making it one of the most recent Australian birds to be identified. The type specimen was gathered on a collecting trip funded by Major Harold Wesley Hall, after whom the bird is named.

name: Hardhead
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Usually silent, but males have a soft, wheezy whistle and 'whirr'. females have a loud rattling 'gaark' call.
did_you_know: Hardheads dive for their food and can swim up to 40 metres under water, using their feet to propel them.

name: Hoary-headed Grebe
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Hoary-headed Grebe is usually silent, occasionally making rolling gutteral or soft churring sounds.
did_you_know: The Hoary-headed Grebe may have been allowed to spread into the previously unsuitable arid inland areas of Australia, with the increased availability of water after the construction of artificial dams, reservoirs and sewage farms.

name: Hooded Plover
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: A quiet piping call and a deep 'chook-chook' call.
did_you_know: The incubation period (30 days) of the Hooded Plover is the longest of the Australasian-breeding plovers.

name: Hooded Robin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Quiet trills, occasional piping whistles.
did_you_know: Hooded Robins may have 'helpers' at their nest: other members of the group that help feed the nestlings and fledglings.

name: Horsfield's Bronze-Cuckoo
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Descending, high-pitched whistle:'fee-ew' or 'tseeeeuw'. Also: 'chirrup' like sparrow or pipit.
did_you_know: Cuckoos are very noisy during the breeding season but are mainly silent at other times of the year.

name: Horsfield's Bushlark
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Rich, varied, tinkling song that includes mimicry.
did_you_know: During breeding season the Horsfield's Bushlark calls loudly while flying high in an undulating flight.

name: House Sparrow
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: House Sparrows give a variety of chirruping and twittering notes. The most typical call is a harsh double-noted "chiisck" or "cherrup".
did_you_know: House Sparrows are actually in decline in their native Europe. Over the last 25 years in the UK the species has declined by 62% and is now red-listed as a species of high conservation concern.

name: Inland Dotterel
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Flight call is a guttural trill , 'krroot' or 'krrr', but usually quiet.
did_you_know: Inland Dotterels are often seen at night on favoured stretches of dirt roads in the outback. They are mainly nocturnal, being generally inactive during the day and feeding at night.

name: Inland Thornbill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Similar to the Brown Thornbill but harsher. It has a spirited territorial song and a high-pitched 'see-see' contact call, and will mimic other birds.
did_you_know: Inland Thornbills, unlike other thornbills, carry their tails cocked, almost like a fairy-wren.

name: Jacky Winter
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The call is clear and carries far, a rapid 'chwit-chwit-chwit-peter-peter-peter'.
did_you_know: The Jacky Winter often decorates the outside of its nest with bits of bark or lichen, bound with spider web, making it look just like the branch it is built on.

name: Kelp Gull
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: A distinctive, strident repeated 'ee-ah', also a wide variety of raucous and yelping notes.
did_you_know: The yelping 'yo-yo-yo-yo' call of the Kelp Gull is used in many films with coastal or marine scenes.

name: King Penguin
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Adults have a loud, polysyllabic trumpeting call when displaying, and a soft 'cooing' when locating other King Penguins on land or mostly at sea. The call of King Penguin chicks is a modulated whistle.
did_you_know: The plumage of a penguin forms a complete, water-resistant sheath necessary for survival in cold seas. Every year, following breeding, the old plumage must be completely replaced.

name: King Quail
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: King Quail have quite a variety of calls. While fairly silent outside the breeding season, one of the best indicators of its presence is a high-pitched three-note call, which has a low volume and is uttered monotonously near sun set. It may be heard all d
did_you_know: King Quail were introduced a number of times in Victoria and may have been released in South Australia. However there appear to be none living now in South Australia. They were first discovered in the Kimberleys area in 1974.

name: Large-billed Scrubwren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Penetrating 'chew' or 'cheer', twitterings while feeding. Also mimics thornbills.
did_you_know: In south-eastern Australia, the Large-billed Scrub-wren rarely builds its own nest. Instead it takes over old or disused nests of other birds, particularly that of its larger relative, the Yellow-throated Scrub-wren , sometimes putting down a new lining over abandoned or infertile eggs.

name: Latham's Snipe
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The alarm call, given when flying off, is 'krek krek'.
did_you_know: When breeding in Japan, Latham's Snipe have spectacular display flights and are called 'Thunder Birds' for the drumming noise made by their outer tail feathers.

name: Laughing Dove
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Advertising call is a soft, bubbling cu-cu, cu-oo or crucu-cu-cucoo. The birds also give a more hurried display call.
did_you_know: The common name is derived from the laughing character of the call while the specific component of the scientific name (senegalensis) has reference to the country, Senegal, where the bird originally described was caught.

name: Laughing Kookaburra
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: The chuckling voice that gives this species its name is a common and familiar sound throughout the bird's range. The loud 'koo-koo-koo-koo-koo-kaa-kaa-kaa' is often sung in a chorus with other individuals. The Laughing Kookaburra also has a shorter 'koooa
did_you_know: The Laughing Kookaburra is not really laughing when it makes its familiar call. The cackle of the Laughing Kookaburra is actually a territorial call to warn other birds to stay away.

name: Leaden Flycatcher
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Clear, loud repeated whistling: 'too-whit' or 'too-whee'; also, harsh rattles and buzzes
did_you_know: Flycatchers have small rictal bristles around their bills. These are modified feathers that act as sensors to help the bird capture flying insects.

name: Lesser Sand Plover
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The usual call is a soft and melodious trill, generally uttered in flight.
did_you_know: Lesser Sand Plovers sometimes take crabs which they catch in the water and carry them to dry ground where they pound them against the earth to dismember them before swallowing.

name: Letter-winged Kite
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A harsh rasping "karr, karr, karr". Alarm call "keek, keek, keek".
did_you_know: The Letter-winged Kite's flight feathers are almost owl-like, being soft and frayed on the trailing edges. This allows them to fly silently on quiet nights, as they seek their rodent prey

name: Lewin's Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The strong 'machine gun' like rattling notes of Lewin's Honeyeater are heard over long distances and reveal its presence in an area.
did_you_know: The tip of the Lewin's Honeyeater's tongue is divided into four tiny sections which resemble a feathery 'paintbrush' allowing it to lap up large quantities of nectar at a time.

name: Little Black Cormorant
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Little Button-quail
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The Little Button-quail has a loud booming call, "oo-ah" or 'coo-oo", usually uttered at night. This can go on for several minutes at a time. It also utters a squeaking call, consisting of two or three "chip-chip-chip" notes when flushed.
did_you_know: In captivity if the enclosure is too small these birds can become agressive. Males may fight each others offspring. The female may kill the offsping so that male will remate, and the female may also kill the male.

name: Little Corella
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: The scientific name for Little Corella, Cacatua sanguinea , means 'Blood-stained Cockatoo' and refers to the dark pink markings between the eye and the bill.

name: Little Crow
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Main call a short sharp, nasal and monotonous nark-nark-nark-nark, or quark-quark
did_you_know: Little Crows behead caterpillars before eating them.

name: Little Curlew
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The usual call in flight is a soft 'tchew, tchew, tchew' raising slightly in pitch; also, harsh alarm calls.
did_you_know: Near Darwin, Little Curlews may gather in really large flocks on playing fields, in gardens and on airports when they first arrive from the north, dispersing when the Wet Season begins.

name: Little Eagle
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Very vocal, especially when breeding, with whistles, chatters, whines and squeals.
did_you_know: Australia has only two 'booted' eagles, the Wedge-tailed and the Little Eagles. Their legs are heavily feathered, giving the effect of trousers with stout solid legs. Other raptors have bare legs, which appear slimmer.

name: Little Egret
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: At the nest the Little Egret utters numerous bubbling and croaking sounds.
did_you_know: The Little Egret will spread one or both of its wings to shade the water while stalking prey.

name: Little Friarbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Noisy, harsh calls. Also some musical 'che-weep, chewip, chewip, chew-will, che-will' notes give in breeding season.
did_you_know: Unlike other friarbirds, the Little Friarbird has no casque (bump) on its bill.

name: Little Grassbird
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Plaintive three-note call: 'tu-peeeee-peeeee'; also variety of rapid chattering notes.
did_you_know: The Little Grassbird will move into temporary swamplands after rains in inland areas.

name: Little Lorikeet
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: short, sharp, high screech - 'zit' or 'zit-zit'.
did_you_know: The Little Lorikeet is Australia's smallest lorikeet. Its species name, pusilla, means tiny.

name: Little Penguin
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: On land at night Little Penguins are noisy, particularly before and during breeding. They also call intermittently at sea, their yapping sounding, like a small dog. This is often the best indication of their presence. Calls help maintain contact between s
did_you_know: At 40 cm - 45 cm tall and weighing 1 kg, the Little Penguin is the smallest of the world's 17 penguins. In contrast, the largest species of penguin, the Emperor Penguin Aptenodytes forsteri , is 1 - 1.3 m high with adult males weighing up to 38 kg.

name: Little Pied Cormorant
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Little Raven
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Gutteral  kar kar kar kar kar and ark ark ark ark.
did_you_know: Agressively defends small territory around nest.

name: Little Tern
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Varied; common calls include an abrupt 'jeep' and a frantic 'kee-kee-kee'.
did_you_know: Occasionally pairs of Little Terns can still be seen diving for fish in Sydney Harbour, where their high pitched calls attract attention. Flocks of as many as 1000 or more birds have been seen on the estuary of the Hunter River and other places on the coast.

name: Little Wattlebird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Loud clucking and distinctive unmusical calls.
did_you_know: The Little Wattlebird is the smallest of the wattlebirds.

name: Long-billed Corella
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: A loud, quavering, two-syllable 'wulluk-wulluk' or 'cadillac-cadillac', as well as a harsh screech.
did_you_know: The scientific name for the genus that includes corellas, Cacatua , comes from the Malay word for a cockatoo: 'kakatuwah'. It means 'a vice', referring to their powerful bills.

name: Magpie Goose
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Magpie-lark
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The 'pee-o-wit' or 'pee-wee' call is frequently given as a duet, each bird raising its wings in turn, and has given rise to the colloquial name of Peewee.
did_you_know: The Magpie-lark's mud nest seems to link it closely with the mud-nest builders of the Family Corcoracidae, the White-winged Chough, and the Apostlebird. But it actually belongs in the Family Dicruridae (Monarchs, Fantails, and Drongos).

name: Major Mitchell's Cockatoo
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Unspecified
