did_you_know: The species name,  leadbeateri, of the Major Mitchell's Cockatoo commemorates Benjamin Leadbeater (1760 – 1837), a London natural history merchant who supplied specimens to the British Museum.

name: Mangrove Gerygone
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Mangrove Gerygones often appear comfortable around humans. Not easily startled.

name: Marsh Sandpiper
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The call varies from a musical 'tu-ee-u tu-ee-u' to a soft 'tew', and metallic sharp 'yip tchik'. The alarm call is rather like that of the Black-winged Stilt.
did_you_know: The Marsh Sandpiper will often follow other birds such as ducks to take advantage of the insects they stir up when they are feeding. At other times they sit quietly and are very easily overlooked.

name: Masked Lapwing
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A loud "kekekekekekekek".
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Masked Owl
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A deep, rasping screech.
did_you_know: The Masked Owl is Australia's largest Tyto owl.

name: Masked Woodswallow
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Musical soft twittering or chattering like those of a miner.
did_you_know: In cold or windy conditions Masked Woodswallows sometimes cluster or huddle together on a branch or wire.

name: Mistletoebird
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Very high-pitched single note; also repeated three-note song, warbles and some mimicry.
did_you_know: In cold weather, the Mistletoebird can undergo torpor, which is the slowing down of bodily functions to conserve energy.

name: Mulga Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Mulga Parrots are not particularly noisy. There is a contact call, described as a soft whistle, repeated 3 or 4 times, and there is a soft chattering call which is  only given occasionally while feeding.
did_you_know: Mulga Parrots are monogamous and in captivity birds that pair up when young are more successful breeders. In one case when the mates of two pairs were swapped the males called continuously to their old mates, who were in neighbouring cages, and ignored the new females.

name: Musk Duck
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Musk Ducks have legs that are placed far back on the body to help them swim and dive, making them clumsy walkers. So, unlike many other duck species, they are very rarely seen on land, preferring to stay in the water.

name: Musk Lorikeet
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The usual contact call is a shrill metallic screech, higher than the Rainbow Lorikeet, in flight and when perched. They constantly chatter when feeding.
did_you_know: Musk Lorikeets are gregarious, often mixing with other parrots when feeding, including Scaly-breasted Lorikeets , Little Lorikeets and Swift Parrots.

name: Nankeen Kestrel
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Extensive surveys placed the Nankeen Kestrel in the top ten most commonly seen birds; it was recorded in 95% of the survey sites located across the whole of Australia.

name: Nankeen Night-Heron
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A loud croak, often at night
did_you_know: The common name of the Nankeen Night Heron arose in early colonial times from the colour of nankeen, a cotton cloth from China.

name: New Holland Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The voice comprises a loud 'chik', a fainter 'pseet' and some chattering notes. If danger, such as a bird of prey approaches, a group of honeyeaters will join together and give a loud alarm call.
did_you_know: With long, slender beaks and a tongue which can protrude well beyond the end of their beaks, New Holland Honeyeaters are able to probe for nectar in the deep flowers of Banksias and Grevilleas.

name: Noisy Friarbird
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Noisy, harsh and discordant; deep honking sound: 'tobacco' or 'four o'clock'. Also a sharp 'owk owk'.
did_you_know: The Noisy Friarbird has a naked head and a large casque (bump) on its bill.

name: Noisy Miner
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A loud 'pwee pwee pwee' and a piping 'pee pee pee' when alarmed
did_you_know: Despite their moderate size, Noisy Miners aggressively attack larger birds such as hawks and kookaburras. These attacks may be so vigorous that most other birds are excluded from an area occupied by Noisy Miners.

name: Noisy Pitta
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Has a variety of calls.  Commonest is a loud, far carrying  "want-a-watch" or "walk-to walk". Also a loud, mournful "keow".
did_you_know: These birds use anvils to break up food such as snails, which are its favourite food. Anvils can be a polished stone stuck in the ground, a tree stump, or even a broken bottle. Some anvils are used for years.

name: Northern Mallard
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Classic duck's 'quack'. Males also have wheezy 'raehb' call.
did_you_know: The specific name for the Mallard - platyrhynchos - means 'flat billed'. This refers to its classic 'duck' bill, which is adapted for feeding in water, with grooves called lamellae that help to grip vegetation and filter out water.

name: Northern Rosella
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A variety of calls: a pinging call; a bell-like piping; a chattering, given when feeding in trees; and a rapid succession of high pitched notes described as "trin-se, trinsee".
did_you_know: Northern Rosellas are not good cage birds, being hard to maintain, expecially in cooler climates. This also can make them very expensive. They are aggressive to other birds and to humans and are not very vocal.

name: Nutmeg Mannikin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A variety of calls but usually a 'Ki-ki-te-te' with the first part almost inaudible.
did_you_know: The Nutmeg Mannikin was introduced into Sydney and Brisbane in the late 1920s or early 1930s.

name: Olive Whistler
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Sweet, powerful increasing 'cho cho cho cho' and other musical calls.
did_you_know: The Olive Whistler may have the most rich and musical calls of all the whistlers.

name: Olive-backed Oriole
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Repeated, rolling 'ori-ori-oriole'.
did_you_know: Olive-backed Orioles are excellent mimics of other birds, and are also 'ventriloquists', meaning they can 'throw' their voices to sound like they are calling from somewhere else.

name: Orange Chat
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: High pitched metallic rasp. Single chirp uttered in flight.
did_you_know: Orange Chats sometimes nest three or more times in a year, depending on seasonal conditions, and do not breed at all in times of drought.

name: Orange-bellied Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Feeding can be accompanied by a soft warbling, and the contact call uttered in flight is a sharp 'tzit' repeated every few seconds. Most distinctive is the alarm call it makes when flushed, a unique 'buzzing', described as 'metallic' and 'explosive'
did_you_know: The Orange-bellied Parrot breeds only in Tasmania, with most of the population migrating to Victoria and South Australia in the winter.

name: Orange-footed Scrubfowl
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Variety of chuckles and Screams, okok ok ok owwwwwk owwwwwwk
did_you_know: Maintain territories excluding single birds of same species.

name: Oriental Plover
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A distinctive, irregularly repeated and soft 'peet', 'tick' or 'tink'.
did_you_know: The Oriental Plover migrates from Mongolia and Manchuria in China to Australia via south east Asia.

name: Pacific Baza
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A double cry 'ee-tui, ee-tui' or 'whee-choo, whee-choo' the second note lower.
did_you_know: The Pacific Baza has golden-yellow, domed eyes which are placed on the sides of its head. This gives it excellent side vision, useful for finding mantids among the leaves.

name: Pacific Black Duck
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Pacific Golden Plover
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Clear and melodic: "Quee"
did_you_know: The Pacific Golden Plover flies further than any other bird on their annual migration other than the Arctic Tern. The tern, being an oceanic bird, can feed in the water while the plover cannot.

name: Pacific Gull
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
call_description: A shouted 'ow-ow', muffled 'awk-awk'.
did_you_know: The Pacific Gull has a curious habit of dropping turban shells and other molluscs, especially limpets and mussels, from a height onto a rock in order to break them open. On some islands and headlands, this has resulted in the formation of 'middens' of shell fragments that could be mistaken for ancient natural beach deposits.

name: Painted Button-quail
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A booming call similar to a Common Bronzewing, used in courtship and between pairs that have lost contact while foraging.
did_you_know: The female is larger and more colourful than the male, which is probably related to their breeding role-reversal.

name: Painted Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Main call is loud whistled 'georgie-georgie...'. Other calls include a throaty 'chur' at the nest and plaintive alarm calls.
did_you_know: Male Painted Honeyeaters give display flights during breeding season, flying steeply upwards from a high perch then descending quickly to another tree, singing the whole time. These flights help the males advertise their territory, attract a mate and repel other males.

name: Pale-headed Rosella
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: The call is similar to that of the Eastern Rosella: 'kwik, kwik' calling in flight, or when perched a high pitched rapid 'pi-pi-pi-pi-pi' and soft chattering.
did_you_know: Even though it is brightly coloured, the Pale-headed Rosella is very well-camouflaged when feeding amongst leaves in the canopy of trees.

name: Pale-yellow Robin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Quieter than the Eastern Yellow Robin. Repeated squeaks, 'seee-seee-seee-seee-seee-seee'.
did_you_know: The Pale-yellow Robin can be found in groups of one dominant male, one or two females and one to two subordinate males, which may be related to the adults. These subordinate males help bring food to the young and breeding females and help to defend the group's territory.

name: Pallid Cuckoo
call_description: A loud, ascending whistle 'too-too-too..', The call is often repeated incessantly, and gave rise to the name of Brainfever-bird.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Paradise Riflebird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A loud rasping 'yaaa-a-a-ss'
did_you_know: Paradise Riflebirds have the unusual habit of draping cast-off snake skins on the rims of nests. It is not known if the snake skins are for purely decorative purposes or whether they are also useful for scaring off potential nest robbers.

name: Peaceful Dove
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A musical 'doodle-doo' repeated often and a loud 'coo-lo-lue'.
did_you_know: When courting, the male Peaceful Dove puts on quite a display of bowing and dipping. He drops his chest and bobs his fully-fanned tail high, giving a 'coo' call.

name: Pectoral Sandpiper
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A hoarse dry reedy chirrup or grating trrip-trrip when flushed, becoming harsher and louder if alarmed
did_you_know: When disturbed Pectoral Sandpipers may freeze or fly zigzag before dropping to cover.

name: Peregrine Falcon
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Loud, shrill, repeated: 'hek-ek-ek', with females lower-pitched than males.
did_you_know: The Peregrine Falcon is one of the fastest birds of prey, swooping down at speeds of up to 300 km/h.

name: Pheasant Coucal
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Deep, hollow 'oop-oop-oop-oop'; also a metallic tapping call.
did_you_know: The Pheasant Coucal is the only Australian cuckoo to build its own nest. It also lives and nests on the ground, unlike other cuckoos.

name: Pied Butcherbird
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The Pied Butcherbird's voice is a beautiful, melodious fluting, sometimes given in turn by several individuals.
did_you_know: Many people consider the Pied Butcherbird to be the best singer of all Australia's birds.

name: Pied Cormorant
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Pied Currawong
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: The main call is a loud "currawong", which gives the bird its name. Other frequent sounds include deep croaks and a wolf whistle.
did_you_know: Pied Currawongs are known for their distinctive, loud and ringing calls which can be far-reaching throughout their territories.

name: Pied Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: A mournful whistled 'tee-titee-tee-tee'.
did_you_know: The highly visible black and white markings of male Pied Honeyeaters are displayed during breeding season with acrobatic aerial flights and by tail-spreading when perched in a prominent location.

name: Pied Imperial-Pigeon
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A variety of calls, including a loud, low-pitched moaning "coo-woo", "moo-oop", or "up-oooo"; and a display call, used in courtship and aggression, described as a loud, bellowing low-pitched "coo-hoo-hoo" or "oom-oom-oom".
did_you_know: The Pied Imperial-Pigeon appears to be the first Australian bird referred to by Europeans. Diego de Prado, on Luis Vaez de Torres' voyage which passed through Torres Strait, recorded seeing there "plenty of very large pigeons all white". This was in 1606.

name: Pilotbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Loud, ringing whistled song with rising end
did_you_know: The species was given its unusual name by early settlers who noticed that it often accompanied feeding Superb Lyrebirds.

name: Pink Robin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Chattering short trill 'chwit-tr-tr-tr-tr', rather wren-like.
did_you_know: The beautiful nest of the Pink Robin is usually decorated with pieces of moss and lichen from the shrub or tree in which it is built.

name: Pink-eared Duck
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: A musical chirruping sound that is unusual for a duck, both while in flight and on water. When fighting, this call becomes almost continuous trilling.
did_you_know: Pink-eared Ducks often feed in head-to-tail pairs swimming in a circle, which concentrates small organisms in a rotating column of water.

name: Plains-wanderer
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Plains-wanderer has a number of calls: a repeated, low pitched "oo"; a soft "chuck" when calling chicks when danger threatens; a gentle "irr-irr" to soothe chicks; a "pie-pie-pie" to summon chicks.
did_you_know: Although the Plains-wanderer is similar to Button-quails, it has a number of quite different features and is the only species in the bird family Pedionomidae.  It is more closely related to shorebirds such as sandpipers than it is to quail; in fact its closest relatives may be the South American seedsnipe.  Pedionomus is Greek for "haunting the fields".

name: Plumed Whistling-Duck
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Loud sibilant whistle
did_you_know: The whistling-ducks are monomorphic (sexes the same colour) but males tend to be slightly larger, with longer plumes.

name: Powerful Owl
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Common adult deep, double hoot: 'woo-hoo' (Fred Van Gessel). Chick 'trilling' contact and begging call (Ed McNabb)
did_you_know: The Powerful Owl is Australia's largest owl.

name: Purple Swamphen
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: A loud, penetrating 'kee-ow', as well as some softer clucking between members of a group while feeding.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Purple-crowned Lorikeet
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Contact call a distinct buzzing "tsit-tsit-tsit" or a thin quick "zit" or "zit-zit".  When feeding they engage in sharp metallic chattering, and they call loudly and continuously in flight when alarmed.
did_you_know: Purple-crowned Lorikeets form monogamous couples and are never far apart. Both prepare their nesting hollow and it has been observed in captivity that the male spends a lot of time in the nest box with the female.

name: Rainbow Bee-eater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A liquid 'prrp prrp' given in flight.
did_you_know: The Rainbow Bee-eater rubs bees and wasps against its perch to remove their stings before eating them.

name: Rainbow Lorikeet
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Frequent screeching and chattering.
did_you_know: The Rainbow Lorikeet was abundant around Sydney until the late 19th century, but was rare in Sydney between then and 1950. It is now highly abundant again across Sydney.

name: Red Knot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Single birds are usually silent, but flocks may give a low 'knutt' call.
did_you_know: Little is known about their migration flights, but evidence suggests that some Red Knots fly non-stop across the West Pacific Ocean from north-eastern Asia.

name: Red Wattlebird
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Several distinctive but unmusical calls including coughs, a harsh 'yac a yac' and a loud 'chok'.
did_you_know: The Red Wattlebird is the second largest honeyeater in Australia (the Tasmanian Yellow Wattlebird is the largest). They can display domineering and often aggressive behaviour towards other birds intruding on their territory.

name: Red-backed Fairy-wren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The call is a weak high-pitched reeling song, soft and unobstrusive, often only heard from quite close.
did_you_know: This is the smallest of the Fairy-wrens and is sometimes known as the Elfin Wren.

name: Red-browed Finch
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Short, high-pitched whistles.
did_you_know: The Red-browed Finch is one of only a very few small Australian birds that can be attracted to bird feeders.

name: Red-browed Treecreeper
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Red-browed Treecreeper has five known calls. There is a "chatter" given by one bird which is answered by a ""retort", a grating sound, a shrill call and a "hiss". The "chatter" is the most common  call, described as "a rapid, slightly descending succe
did_you_know: Climacteris in the Red-browed Treecreeper's scientific name comes from  the Greek word for the rung of a ladder, referring to its tree climbing habits. Erythrops refers to its red eye-patch.

name: Red-capped Parrot
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: In flight, a grating 2 syllable "krukk-rak" or "crrr-uk" and shrieks when alarmed.
did_you_know: Young birds learn to feed in a special way from their parents, using their spectacular long bill. They hold a large capsule with a foot, rotating the food and manipulating the long upper bill to neatly extract seeds.

name: Red-capped Plover
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Varied abrupt 'tik', often repeated.
did_you_know: Both parents share the nest duties and if the nest is threatened the Red-capped Plovers will try several distraction methods, including feigning injury by dragging a wing to lead predators away.

name: Red-capped Robin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Males sing with characteristic dry, repeated trill: 'dit-dit-drr-it'. Both sexes have a 'tick' call.
did_you_know: Both male and female Red-capped Robins respond strongly to playback of their species' song by flying to the source, flitting about in agitation, and sometimes replying with their own song.

name: Red-kneed Dotterel
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Alarm call a rapid: 'wit-wit'.
did_you_know: The Red-kneed Dotterel can run very fast and often uses this ability to escape predators.

name: Red-necked Avocet
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Musical 'toot toot'; also, yelps and wheezes.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Red-necked Stint
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Calls include: 'prip' contact call and alarm 'chit'.
did_you_know: During studies on waders, two juvenile Red-necked Stints aged only 44 and 50 days were found about 2000 km from their breeding grounds.

name: Red-rumped Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A two-syllable whistle: 'suweet-weet'.
did_you_know: Many parrots, including the Red-rumped Parrot, found in areas which have not formerly been part of their natural range may be escaped cage birds.

name: Red-tailed Black-Cockatoo
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Usual contact call loud rolling metallid kree or krurr-rr, uttered in flight or when perched; also sharp krur-rak in alarm; all calls loud, harsh and far-carrying.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Red-whiskered Bulbul
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The call, a characteristic descending musical whistle, often indicates a bird's presence long before it is seen.
did_you_know: The Red-whiskered Bulbul is a native species of China but was introduced to Australia in the early 1900s.

name: Red-winged Parrot
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The Red-winged Parrot usually calls in flight with a sharp metallic 'crillik, crillik' and a harsh shrieking 'chik-chik-chik' in alarm.
did_you_know: The courtship display of the Red-winged Parrot is very colourful: the male circles the favoured female, then lowers his wings to expose the blue patch on his lower back, which is usually hidden. He holds his feathers close to his body and contracts his pupils.

name: Regent Bowerbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Low chattering, wheezy calls. ventriloquial mimicry.
did_you_know: The male Regent Bowerbird's plumage can take from two to five years to develop to full maturity.

name: Regent Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Quiet, melodious calls; can mimic larger honeyeaters such as wattlebirds and friarbirds.
did_you_know: The Regent Honeyeater has become a 'flagship species' for conservation issues in the box-ironbark forest region of Victoria and New South Wales. Birds Australia is helping to conserve Regent Honeyeaters as part of its Woodland Birds for Biodiversity project. To find out more or get involved go to the WBFB project page .

name: Regent Parrot
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A loud and harsh 'carrak, carrak'. Also soft twittering contact calls.
did_you_know: Male Regent Parrots feed the female during incubation, so they depend on a good food source near the nesting tree hollow. The declining eastern population needs remnant mallee patches near their tree hollows. In the west, Regent Parrots benefit from agricultural crops and grain. The eastern population has declined, depending on stream-side trees for nesting and limited nearby mallee for feeding. It is listed as Endangered in New South Wales.

name: Restless Flycatcher
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Continuous whirring or rasping hisses when hovering.
did_you_know: Another common name for the Restless Flycatcher is 'Scissors Grinder', for its rasping or hissing call when hovering.

name: Rock Dove
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: The most common call is a moaning 'cooo-rooooo-cu-cu'.
did_you_know: The Rock Dove, often refered to as the 'Feral Pigeon', is one of three introduced pigeon and dove species to Australia. Rock Doves originated in Europe, Asia and Africa and are often bred as racing pigeons.

name: Rock Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: A plaintive but piercing two note call 'tsit-tseet', repeated frequently in flight; soft chattering when feeding.
did_you_know: The Rock Parrot has the dubious honour of having the least colourful plumage of any Australian parrot. Greys and browns, dull yellow and green predominate but when seen in the field, it appears deceptively bright, due mainly to its mostly yellow tail and undertail-coverts.

name: Rockwarbler
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A shrill, slight mournful 'goodbye' song and a penetrating 'pink' call, along with other rasping notes.
did_you_know: The Rockwarbler nests in caves, usually in near or complete darkness.

name: Rose Robin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Male has pretty, trilled song: 'dick-dick-diddit-deer-deer-deer'; both sexes 'tick'.
did_you_know: The Rose Robin is the most acrobatic of the red robins, catching flying insects high in trees.

name: Rose-crowned Fruit-Dove
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The birds are often detected by their call, a loud 'boo-uk-boo' or 'woo-up-woo'.
did_you_know: Rose-crowned Fruit-Doves feed on fruit high in the canopy and can be very hard to see. Often they are only detected by their calls or the sound of fruit dropping to the ground.

name: Royal Spoonbill
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Grunts, growls and soft honks. Also makes non-vocal sounds such as bill-snapping and 'wing-woofing' during aggressive displays.
did_you_know: The Royal Spoonbill can feed faster and on larger prey than the Yellow-billed Spoonbill, as it has a shorter, broader bill with more papillae (touch receptors) inside the spoon.

name: Ruddy Turnstone
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: In flight, a rapid 'trik-tuk-tuk-tuk. They are noisy and quarrelsome, with a sharp 'kittick' or rapid chuckling 'tak-a-tuk-tuk'.
did_you_know: Ruddy Turnstones use their strong, wedge-shaped bills to turn over rocks and seaweed, looking for small sand-hoppers or crustaceans sheltering underneath.

name: Rufous Fantail
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Thin, ascending whistles; also a single or double 'chip'.
did_you_know: The Rufous Fantail is found in wetter, denser habitats than the related Grey Fantail.

name: Rufous Owl
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Soft, low-pitched, measured double hoot woo-hoo
did_you_know: The Rufous Owl is the only exclusively tropical owl in Australia.

name: Rufous Songlark
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Almost continuous in the breeding season, the song of the Rufous Songlark has been described as joyful, metallic, pleasant and musical. There is also a whip-like sound included.
did_you_know: During the breeding season the inside of the female Rufous Songlark's mouth is pinkish whereas the inside of the male's mouth becomes black, as does its bill. As males sing almost constantly in breeding season, the black colour may be seen.

name: Rufous Whistler
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A long loud series of ringing notes.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Sacred Kingfisher
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The voice of the Sacred Kingfisher is a loud "ek ek ek ek" repeated continuously throughout breeding season. Birds also give a "kee kee kee" in excitement and a series of chirring, scolding notes when alarmed.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Sanderling
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: In flight, the call is a quick 'twick twick twick' and soft twittering in flocks.
did_you_know: he Sanderling is a remarkable long-distance flier and builds up huge reserves of fat for fuel for the journey before migrating. Flights may be 5000 kilometres.

name: Satin Bowerbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Satin Bowerbirds have an amazing variety of sounds, including whistles, buzzing and hissing, as well as mimicry. The male also gives a loud "weeoo".
did_you_know: A male Satin Bowerbird only develops his wonderful satiny sheen after seven years. Up until this time, the males possess the same plumage and colouring as the females.

name: Satin Flycatcher
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Sharp, metallic, rising whistle: 'chwee-wip, chwee-wip, chwee-wip'; also harsh grating buzzes, repeated often.
did_you_know: All the Myiagra flycatchers have short crests which are most often erected when calling from perches, while also swaying or flicking their tails from side to side.

name: Scaly-breasted Lorikeet
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: High-pitched rolling screeches.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Scarlet Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Males have a silvery tinkling song, which is sung from a prominent perch. Also, 'chiew chiew' contact calls made by both sexes.
did_you_know: Populations of Scarlet Honeyeaters have occasionally exploded suddenly, with larger numbers than usual being reported in a particular area.

name: Scarlet Robin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A repeated, sweet six-note song: 'wee-cheedalee-dalee'.
did_you_know: Scarlet Robins and Flame Robins will defend their territories against each other. Flame Robins are dominant when setting up a breeding territory and may take over part of a Scarlet Robin's permanent territory. But once established, both species have a similar chance of winning disputes.

name: Scarlet-chested Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: a soft twittering, mellow and abrupt, not carrying far.
did_you_know: The Scarlet-chested Parrot has frequently been found far from water. It may obtain sufficient moisture by drinking dew or chewing water-storing plants such as Calandrinia which grows in the sandy mulga country.

name: Scrubtit
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Quiet most of the time, but with a loud whistle.  Described as a "sweet little song.. with modest tinkling notes". Other calls are a soft "peep" or "cheep" and an alarm call described as "to-wee-to", or "to-wee-to-wee".
did_you_know: The Scrubtit was first described scientifically by John Gould back in 1855, who placed it amongst the thornbills.

name: Sharp-tailed Sandpiper
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Dry 'wit-wit'; also, crackling warbles and musical twitterings.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Shining Bronze-Cuckoo
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Shining Bronze-Cuckoo chicks are blind and mostly naked when they hatch and their yolk-sack is still visible beneath their skin until they are about 4 days old. They eject the other contents of the host nest within 24 to 96 hours of hatching .

name: Short-tailed Shearwater
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Silver Gull
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: The most common call is a harsh 'kwee-aarr'.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Silvereye
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The contact call, a thin "psip", is given persistently.
did_you_know: Although one of Australia's smallest birds, the Silvereye is capable of travelling great distances during migration, with Silvereyes from the most southerly regions of Tasmania travelling all the way up to Southern Queensland.

name: Singing Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: A large range of clear, noisy calls, usually lively and melodious: 'prrip, prrip'. Dawn choruses may last for an hour, starting before sunrise.
did_you_know: In Western Australia it can be common to have a male Singing Honeyeater every 50 m along a suburban street, with each male's territory centred around a flowering food source.

name: Sooty Oystercatcher
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A loud piercing, piping cry: 'kervee-kervee-kervee'.
did_you_know: The Sooty Oystercatcher is the only all-black shorebird in Australia.

name: Sooty Shearwater
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: usually silent at sea but sometimes calls whenb flying over colonies. It calls a lot when on the ground and in the burrow. Its main called is described as a loud, rythmically repeated "der-rer-ah" or high-pitched "coo-roo-ah".
did_you_know: Commercial harvesting of Sooty Shearwaters occurs around Stewart Island, New Zealand. It is the only species allowed to be sold commercially and is used mostly for food, but some are used for making soap and lubricating oil.

name: Southern Boobook
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A distinctive 'boo-book' or 'mo-poke'.
did_you_know: The Southern Boobook, often refered to a 'Mopoke' after its call, is Australia's smallest owl.

name: Southern Cassowary
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: The calls of the Southern Cassowary consist of an assortment of rumblings and grunts. These calls are often heard long before the bird is seen, and are usually given in response to the sight of potential danger.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Southern Emu-wren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Soft reedy chirp: 'prip prip'; males have short descending song like fairy-wrens but higher-pitched.
did_you_know: The emu-wrens are named for their six wispy, emu-like tail feathers.

name: Southern Whiteface
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Continual rapid twittering on one note, flight call is a brisk 'wit, wit-awit'.
did_you_know: The Southern Whiteface  forages in groups of 10-15 (or larger!) and mixes with other feeding species such as Yellow-rumped Thornbills, covering ground in short half-hops, one foot in front of the other, picking up food as they go.

name: Spangled Drongo
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A variety of sounds, including some distinctive metallic notes like a stretched wire being plucked, and occasional mimicry of other bird species.
did_you_know: Spangled Drongos frequently flock together to 'hawk' flying insects for food.

name: Speckled Warbler
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The call of the Speckled Warbler has been described as a soft musucal whistle that is "sweet, cheerful and pleasing". It is a good mimic, including parts of the calls of other birds. It also has a rasping, scolding call.
did_you_know: The eggs of the Speckled Warbler are a glossy red-brown, leading to unusal local names such as "Chocolate Bird" and "Blood Tit".

name: Spectacled Monarch
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Harsh buzzing, scolding and chattering; also long, quiet 'breer breer breer'.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Spiny-cheeked Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Gargling or bubbling notes and whistles; also, single loud 'tock'. Can mimic other species.
did_you_know: The Spiny-cheeked Honeyeater is one of the frugivorous (fruit-eating) honeyeaters, often following seasonal fruiting patterns; however, it also eats nectar, insects and small vertebrates.

name: Splendid Fairy-wren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: A rapid series of slightly metallic, high-pitched pips that blend into an "undulating" call.
did_you_know: The nest is so small that the female's long tail is bent during incubation.

name: Spotted Dove
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The most common call is a musical "cocoo, crooor".
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Spotted Harrier
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Usually silent, but when breeding may give piercing squeaks and rapid chatter.
did_you_know: Spotted Harriers often build their nest on top of a patch of mistletoe, hidden by foliage. The chosen tree is usually in a patch of other trees or shrubs, rather than in an isolated tree.

name: Spotted Pardalote
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Repeated three-note whistle, the second two notes higher than the first.
did_you_know: The Spotted Pardalote is sometimes known as the "Headache Bird" because of the continuous "sleep-may-be" call it gives during the breeding season.

name: Square-tailed Kite
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Yelping, yeep, yeep, yeep. Also squealing   ee ee ee ee
did_you_know: Does not eat carrion.

name: Straw-necked Ibis
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
call_description: Silent away from nest; grunts or croaks at nest and hoarse rolling calls in flight: 'u-u-uh'.
did_you_know: The Straw-necked Ibis has been called the Farmer's Friend, because it eats crop pests such as grasshoppers and locusts.

name: Striated Heron
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Striated Pardalote
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: A sharp "tchip tchip". Contact calls: soft trills.
did_you_know: Pardalotes generally feed in the canopies of tall eucalypts, making them difficult to see. However, when nesting, they are often oblivious to observers and can be easily seen flying to and from their nesting burrows as they feed in nearby trees.

name: Striated Thornbill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: High-pitched insect-like calls: 'tiziz-tiziz'.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Striped Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Strong-billed Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Loud sharp 'cheep'; also often heard ripping bark.
did_you_know: Unlike other Melithreptus honeyeaters, the Strong-billed Honeyeater is adapted to foraging for insects on the trunks of trees, moving up and down vertically and ripping at the bark to find food.

name: Stubble Quail
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Three main calls.  A loud, whistled and clear “two-to-weep" is heard persistently on moonlit nights soon after a nest is built. Also a loud, often repeated two-note call, described as a loud and sharp “to-weep”. Emits chirps, given when flushed.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Sulphur-crested Cockatoo
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: The most common call is a distinctive loud screech, ending with a slight upward inflection
did_you_know: One of Australia's most popular and iconic birds, the Sulphur-crested Cockatoo, has been known to live up to eighty years of age in captivity.

name: Superb Fairy-wren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The Superb Fairy-wren gives a series of high pitched trills, which are given by both sexes. The male often extends these trills into song.
did_you_know: Male Superb Fairy-wrens have been labelled as 'the least faithful birds in the world'. Females may be courted by up to 13 males in half an hour, and 76% of young are sired by males from outside the social group.

name: Superb Fruit-Dove
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Slow, steady series of 'whoops'. This distinguishes the Superb Fruit-Dove from the Rose-Crowned fruit Dove.
did_you_know: Fruit-Doves are among the most important seed dispersers in Australian tropical and sub-tropical forests.

name: Superb Lyrebird
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Mimicked calls: chainsaws, car engines, dog barks and local native birds. Other calls: a series of whistles and cackling notes that are used as territorial calls, as well as a loud alarm shriek.
did_you_know: About 80% of the Superb Lyrebird's song consists of expert mimicry, with both natural and mechanical sounds imitated and joined together in a rousing medley. Sounds can include anything heard in the bird's immediate surroundings, such as chainsaws, car engines, dog barks and local native birds.

name: Superb Parrot
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Loud 'krak, krrak' contact call; soft twittering from feeding birds. All calls have a distinctive throaty quality.
did_you_know: During the 20-day incubation period and for a week or so after the eggs hatch, the female Superb Parrot is fed entirely by the male, in the nest or nearby.

name: Swamp Harrier
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
call_description: Usually silent, but gives high pitched descending whistle in breeding display.
did_you_know: Swamp Harriers are easily disturbed at the nest and will abandon their eggs and even downy young if approached by people.

name: Swift Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The usual contact call in flight is a loud, metallic 'chit chit' repeated three or four times in succession and soft chattering when feeding.
did_you_know: Swift Parrots breed only in Tasmania, along the eastern coastal strip, the Wellington ranges near Hobart and on Maria and Bruny Islands.

name: Tasmanian Native-hen
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: 14 separate calls have been identified. Characteristic call is a loud rasping "see-saw" and a number of grunts.
did_you_know: The Tasmanian Native-Hen was widespread on the Australian mainland until about 4700 years ago when it became extinct, possibly through predation by newly arrived Dingo and increasing aridity of the continent.

name: Tasmanian Scrubwren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The Tasmanian Scrubwren has three calls. The song call is like a squeaky wheel, and can last a long time. It also uses a soft "peep" call to keep contact with its mate while foraging. The alarm call is a scolding, rasping chatter.
did_you_know: The Tasmanian Scrubwren is known as the alarm bird of the Tasmanian scrub, as it is the first to signal danger.

name: Tasmanian Thornbill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Sweet musical warbling.
did_you_know: Reverend Thomas J. Ewing (d.1876) for whom this bird is named was the headmaster of the Queen's Orphan Schools, Tasmania. John Gould (who first described the bird) stayed with Rev. Ewing during his visit to Tasmania in 1838-39.

name: Tawny Frogmouth
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A soft, deep, continuous, 'ooo-ooo-ooo' sound.
did_you_know: The leading edges of the first primary (wing) feathers of the Tawny Frogmouth are fringed to allow for silent flight.

name: Tawny Grassbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: High pitched descending trill or scolding calls jk jk.
did_you_know: The song by the male is often given from elevated perches and can be heard from a distance of several hundred metres,

name: Tawny-crowned Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A liquid, fluty, mournful call.
did_you_know: One pair of Tawny-crowned Honeayeaters continued to feed their nestlings despite being surrounded by shellfire at an artillery range.

name: Terek Sandpiper
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: When flying, calls 'twit-wit-wit-wit' rising slightly in pitch for each syllable.
did_you_know: Female Terek Sandpipers leave their breeding grounds to migrate in early July, before the males and juveniles, which leave later, mainly in August. Their estimated flight range is 3500 km - 4800 km.

name: Topknot Pigeon
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Occasional sharp screech when feeding; otherwise silent or soft, clear coos when it approaches its nest.
did_you_know: The Topknot Pigeon is the only rainforest pigeon to regularly fly high above the tree canopy.

name: Torresian Crow
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Nasal, staccato caw: 'uk-uk-uk-uk', usually more than three notes. Also harsher 'arr-arr-arr' aggressive call.
did_you_know: The Torresian Crow shuffles its wings when landing at a perch.

name: Tree Martin
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The Tree Martin's call is a twittering sound. They often twitter constantly.
did_you_know: When Tree Martins approach their roosting sites near sunset they may form large flocks, up to 50,000 in one estimate, which rise into the air en-masse, and then dive downwards together to disappear into the vegetation.

name: Turquoise Parrot
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: A high, weak, musical tinkling in flight; also, a faint high twittering call when feeding.
did_you_know: Until the 1880's, the Turquoise Parrot was considered the most common species of parrot in Western Sydney and was one of only two species recorded before 1900 .

name: Varied Sittella
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The contact call is a single 'chip' sometimes developing into a rapid chatter. Flocks call noisily when foraging.
did_you_know: The feet of the Varied Sitella are small but with very long toes for clinging onto branches. They move in spirals down trees, searching for food, and even hang below branches.

name: Varied Triller
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: A distinctive "churring trill" sound. This has also been described as a soft rattling or rolling note, like a pea whistle, or as cicada-like. It also has a somewhat shrill piping call.
did_you_know: The first part the Varied Triller's scientific name, Lalage, comes from a bird mentioned in a large dictionary of unusual Greek words compiled by one Hesychius in the 5th or 6th Century C.E. However Hesychius did not describe this bird.

name: Variegated Fairy-wren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: A mechanical 'triri-tirirrit-tirit-trit-tirrririt-trit-tirrit' call only in the breeding season.
did_you_know: Variegated Fairy-wrens are highly sociable birds, living in communal, territorial groups that always consist of a dominant male and female; the rest of the group are young males and females.

name: Wandering Albatross
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: The Wandering Albatross is the largest of the albatrosses and is the living bird with the greatest wingspan, measuring almost 3.5 m.

name: Wandering Whistling-Duck
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Shrill twittering, whistling, especially noisy with almost incessant whistling when flocks are airborne.
did_you_know: Wandering Whistling-Ducks are gregarious when not breeding, and form large flocks of up to thousands of individuals. They often flock with Plumed Whistling-Ducks.

name: Wedge-tailed Eagle
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: The Wedge-tailed Eagle is Australia's largest living bird of prey and one of the largest eagles in the world

name: Weebill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The voice is "wee bit" or "wee willy weetee".
did_you_know: Weebills are some of Australia's smallest birds, with northern Australian Weebills even smaller than those in the south.

name: Welcome Swallow
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The call is a mixture of twittering and soft warbling notes, and a sharp whistle in alarm.
did_you_know: Welcome Swallows have short bristles at the sides of their mouths which help to guide their food (insects) into their mouths while flying at speed.

name: Western Bowerbird
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Churring, hissing and grating calls, with mimicry of bird calls and other sounds.
did_you_know: Their bowers may be decorated with many things the male finds attractive. The decorations in one bower found near Alice Springs weighed 7.4 kg with 1427 bone fragments, many snail shells, pebbles and bits of glass - and white is right.

name: Western Gerygone
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: A clear sweet silvery song whistled by the males throughout the day
did_you_know: The Western Gerygone tends to be restless in its movements, shaking itself frequently as if its feathers are wet.

name: Western Rosella
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: High pitched, ringing 'quink, quink, quink, quink' and a softer ' whip-a-whee'.
did_you_know: The Western Rosella is the only rosella with yellow cheek patches; others have white or blue patches.

name: Whimbrel
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The commonest call is a far-carrying rippling 'bibibibibibibi'.
did_you_know: A Whimbrel that was banded in New South Wales was re-captured on the Kamchatka Peninsula in Siberia.

name: Whiskered Tern
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Varied; long hoarse 'kerch', 'kerrrk' or abrupt 'kittitt'.
did_you_know: A whole colony of Whiskered Terns will quickly fly to mob or attack a predator or intruder, including humans. Other waterbirds often take advantage of this protection by nesting within the colony, particularly Hoary-headed Grebes. The terns however have been known to prey on the chicks of small grebes.

name: Whistling Kite
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: Loud descending whistle: 'teee-ti-ti'.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: White-bellied Sea-Eagle
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: Distinctive loud "goose-like" honking call, which is heard particularly during the breeding season.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: White-breasted Woodswallow
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Brassy chirps: 'pirrt, pirrt'; loud chattering and quiet twittering; some mimicry.
did_you_know: Although woodswallows have bifurcated (divided) tongues that are adapted for nectar feeding, they tend to feed mainly on insects.

name: White-browed Babbler
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Chattering miaowing; whistled rising 'sweet-sweet-sweet-miaow'. Its alarm call is a brisk 'wit-wit'. The most common call is a contact call 'chuk' while feeding.
did_you_know: White-browed Babblers build communal roosting nests of twigs and sticks, usually in dead or partly living trees. They participate in activities such as dust-bathing, preening and feeding as a group.

name: White-browed Scrubwren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The call is an almost persistent harsh chattering of scalding notes, especially when disturbed. White-browed Scrubwrens are also accomplished mimics.
did_you_know: White-browed Scubwrens are among Australia's most active birds, constantly foraging amongst the leaf-litter of the forest floor for food.

name: White-browed Woodswallow
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Musical: 'chep, chep'; also soft chattering, harsh scoldings and some mimicry.
did_you_know: Woodswalllows roost together in tight clusters at night, as well as during cold weather and storms.

name: White-cheeked Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: Loud clear double whistle, and a brief 'e-chip'. Loud chattering and squabbling in groups, as well as rasping alarm calls. Also snaps bill during chases.
did_you_know: Although very similar In appearance, there is not much competition between White-cheeked and New Holland Honeyeaters, as they choose different perching sites and have different nesting seasons.

name: White-eared Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Deep, slightly metallic voice. Calls included a loud 'chew chew chew' or a two-note: 'tch-tchew, tch-tchew'.
did_you_know: The White-eared Honeyeater is renowned for its habit of collecting hair from people's heads to line its nest.

name: White-faced Heron
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: White-fronted Chat
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Short 'tangs' sounding like a plucked rubber band.
did_you_know: Although they are classified as honeyeaters, White-fronted Chats do not feed on nectar. Instead, they run along the ground feeding on insects. However, they have the same brush-tipped tongues as other members of their family.

name: White-fronted Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Variety of loud calls, including harsh metallic notes and cheerful melodic song: 'pert-peetoo-weet'.
did_you_know: In hot weather, adult White-fronted Honeyeaters may straddle nests to shade their young.

name: White-fronted Tern
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: White-fronted Terns have several calls, from the short 'krek' noise while in the nesting colony that makes the colony very noisy, to the 'rasping yawn' of the alarm call such as when a predator attacks the colony.
did_you_know: Striata is from the Modern Latin word striatus for streaked or striped. The scientific name for the White-fronted Tern comes from the barred upperparts of the juveniles' plumage.

name: White-headed Pigeon
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: A strong 'whook' and a slow mournful repeated 'oom-coo'.
did_you_know: The White-headed Pigeon prefers to feed in the introduced tree species Camphor Laurel.

name: White-naped Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Harsh, churring 'shersh-shersh-shersh' and single note whistle, along with alarm and contact calls.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: White-necked Heron
size: Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
call_description: A loud croak is uttered as an alarm call. Other gutteral calls are uttered at the nest.
did_you_know: Like other herons, the White-necked Heron has a special hinge mechanism at the sixth vertebra that allows them to rapidly extend their folded neck and so catch unwary prey.

name: White-plumed Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The White-plumed Honeyeater is one of the first birds to call in the morning and the last to call in the evening, with several songs e.g. 'chick-ick-o-wee' or 'chirrapo-we-weet, other calls and musical whistles. Also has a piping alarm call.
did_you_know: The White-plumed Honeyeater is one of the first birds to call in the morning and the last to call in the evening.

name: White-throated Gerygone
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Distinctive descending trill.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: White-throated Needletail
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Unspecified
did_you_know: White-throated Needletails are able to fly at great speeds of up to 130 km per hour.

name: White-throated Treecreeper
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Piping, tremulous calls.
did_you_know: The White-throated Treecreeper mainly eats ants.

name: White-winged Black Tern
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Buzzing and rapid short cries ('kik-kik-kik')
did_you_know: White-winged Black terns, along with Black Terns and Whiskered terns C. hybrida, form a group of smallish terns called marsh terns - they all use vegetated wetlands as habitat.

name: White-winged Chough
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: The White-winged Chough is often first noticed by a mournful, descending whistle. If disturbed, it gives a ratchet-like call.
did_you_know: White-winged Choughs live in social clans of about seven to ten individuals and will defend their nest territory during the breeding season with 'wing-waving' displays to deter unwanted intruders.

name: White-winged Fairy-wren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The song consists of a few short introductory notes followed by prolonged reel of up to 4 seconds' duration with regular rise and fall in pitch.  The contact call is a "tsit" or a brief soft reel. The alarm call is an abrupt "tsit"
did_you_know: The White-winged Fairy-wren was first named, 'Merion leucoptere' for the Dirk Hartog Island subspecies, by French naturalists, Quoy and Gaimard, in their publication of 1824. Subspecies Barrow Island ( Malurus leucopterus edouardi ) and Dirk Hartog Island ( Malurus leucopterus leucopterus ) subspecies are listed as vulnerable at the federal level, and rare in Western Australia.

name: White-winged Triller
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Descending 'chiff-chiff-joey-joey-joey'. Very noisy during the breeding season, mainly calling in flight.
did_you_know: Like other members of the Family Campephagidae, White-winged Trillers have an undulating flight and often shuffle re-fold their wings after landing on a branch.

name: Willie Wagtail
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: The Willie Wagtail's call is well-known, often being uttered constantly throughout the night, and is interpreted as "sweet-pretty-creature", though other calls involve more scolding and chattering notes.
did_you_know: The Willie Wagtail is often found in the company of cattle and sheep. They either run behind the moving animal snatching insects as they are disturbed, or sit on the animal's back, darting off to capture a flying insect and then returning to its mobile perch.

name: Wompoo Fruit-Dove
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
call_description: The call is a deep resonant "wollack-a-woo" and, occasionally, a more abrupt "boo".
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Wonga Pigeon
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
call_description: Loud monotonous 'woop woop' calls can be heard up to 2 km away and can be given for hours on end.
did_you_know: Wonga Pigeons make clearly visible 'tracks' by following exactly the same path each time they visit a feeding site.

name: Wood Sandpiper
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: The call is a shrill, whistled 'chiff-iff-iff' and the alarm call is a sharper 'chip' repeated rapidly.
did_you_know: The Wood Sandpiper is wary and nervous and will burst into flight if disturbed, zig-zagging off and calling loudly, then gliding gracefully to ground again.

name: Yellow Thornbill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Harsh, scratchy two-note calls: 'tzid-id' or 'tzid-id, tis-tis'.
did_you_know: Unspecified

name: Yellow Wattlebird
size: Medium (30 cm to 45 cm e.g. pigeon)
Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Loud, harsh and raucous: 'kuk' or 'kukuk'. Calls are 'spat' out, with the bird jerking its head back then forward strongly.
did_you_know: The Yellow Wattlebird is Australia's largest honeyeater.

name: Yellow-billed Spoonbill
size: Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
Very large (> 75 cm e.g. pelican)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: Almost mute; some feeble grunting and also bill-clapping.
did_you_know: Yellow-billed Spoonbills can use much smaller bodies of water than the related Royal Spoonbills.

name: Yellow-faced Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Loud, cheerful calls: series of 'chick-up' notes.
did_you_know: When migrating, the Yellow-faced Honeyeater can be seen in large flocks, with several thousand birds passing every hour in some places.

name: Yellow-plumed Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Markings: obvious streaks, spots and/or showy
call_description: Loud, ringing 'chick-o'wee'; far-carrying alarm chirps and trills.
did_you_know: Groups of Yellow-plumed Honeyeaters may take part in 'corroborrees', where individuals perform wing-fluttering displays and call. Groups may also band together to repel intruders from their own and other bird species, fighting to the point of falling to the ground.

name: Yellow-rumped Thornbill
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Musical, cheery, tinkling song, ending with two clear whistled notes, repeated often.
did_you_know: The Yellow-rumped Thornbill builds a large, double-storeyed nest with a 'false' nest on top.

name: Yellow-tailed Black-Cockatoo
size: Medium to large (45 cm to 60 cm e.g. raven)
Large (60 cm to 75 cm e.g. ibis)
distinctive_features: Cheek: obvious white or coloured patch
call_description: The contact call is a drawn-out "kee-ow". Some screeches are also given.
did_you_know: The Yellow-Tailed Black-Cockatoo is one of six species of Black-Cockatoo in Australia. In recent years it has been in rapid decline because of native habitat clearance, with a loss of food supply and nest sites.

name: Yellow-throated Honeyeater
size: Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Loud 'tonk' calls, also 'pick-em-up' or 'get-a-whip'; aggressive churring and bill-snapping when chasing other birds.
did_you_know: The Yellow-throated Honeyeater can be quite aggressive towards other honeyeaters, as well as other species such as pardalotes, Golden Whistlers and Grey Shrike-thrushes, chasing them away in both breeding and non-breeding seasons.

name: Yellow-throated Miner
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
distinctive_features: Face: distinctively masked or bare skin
call_description: A piping 'pwee-pwee-pwe', similar to Noisy Miners; also harsh calls and chatter.
did_you_know: Flocks of Yellow-throated Miners utter a musical, pre-dawn song.

name: Yellow-throated Scrubwren
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
Small (15 cm to 30 cm e.g. common myna)
call_description: Melodious whistles, harsh chattering; also some mimicry.
did_you_know: The Yellow-throated Scrubwren has been called the Blacknest-bird, for its habit of using black roots to build its domed nest.

name: Yellow-tufted Honeyeater
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: Has a varied single-note contact or alarm call: tsup, shup, jik, chow or scow. Also has various soft notes used as social calls, and a soft 'weet-weet-weet' territorial call.
did_you_know: One sub-species of the Yellow-tufted Honeyeater, known as the Helmeted Honeyeater, is endangered.

name: Zebra Finch
size: Very small (< 15 cm: e.g. sparrow)
call_description: The most common calls are a loud nasal "tiah", often given in flight, and a soft "tet tet" in close contact.
did_you_know: With a time-span of 70 to 80 days from hatching to becoming sexually active, the Zebra Finch is one of the fastest maturing bird species recorded.
